descriptionChirho: To feel regret or remorse after the fact, a change of feeling (not necessarily repentance in the full theological sense of metanoia). Used of the son who regretted refusing to work (Matt 21:29, 32), Judas who felt remorse for betraying Jesus (Matt 27:3), Paul's initial regret over a stern letter (2 Cor 7:8), and God's oath from which he will not change his mind (Heb 7:21). Multilingual glosses consistently render regret/remorse: Arabic nadima, German bereuen, French regretter/se repentir, Hebrew hitcharet/nicham, Hindi pachtatana, Korean huhoe, Spanish arrepentirse.
